rule.label: v2
rule.title: Bounty payout on a working fix (tightened)
rule.rule_text:
Pay the contributor the full bounty if all of the following hold. (1) The
designated check suite named in the bounty listing reports every check passing on
the contributor's final commit; that suite is the sole authority on whether the
fix works, and no other runner, local result, or opinion overrides it. (2) The
suite reports no check failing that was passing on the parent commit; a newly
failing check anywhere in the suite defeats payment even if the reported defect is
closed. (3) Every reproduction path recorded on the issue at the time the bounty
was posted no longer reproduces the defect. If some but not all recorded
reproduction paths are resolved, pay the contributor that fraction of the bounty,
rounded down to the nearest whole unit. (4) The contributor's final commit was
pushed before the cutoff stated in the listing; the cutoff binds the push, not the
completion of the check suite, and delay caused by neither party does not defeat
payment. (5) Where the reported defect is that an operation is too slow, the
listing's stated numeric threshold governs; if the listing states no threshold,
this rule does not determine an outcome. If the designated check suite has not
reported within fourteen days of the push, and no maintainer has stated a
position, pay the full bounty.
rule.normalized: Pay the contributor the full bounty if all of the following hold. (1) The designated check suite named in the bounty listing reports every check passing on the contributor's final commit; that suite is the sole authority on whether the fix works, and no other runner, local result, or opinion overrides it. (2) The suite reports no check failing that was passing on the parent commit; a newly failing check anywhere in the suite defeats payment even if the reported defect is closed. (3) Every reproduction path recorded on the issue at the time the bounty was posted no longer reproduces the defect. If some but not all recorded reproduction paths are resolved, pay the contributor that fraction of the bounty, rounded down to the nearest whole unit. (4) The contributor's final commit was pushed before the cutoff stated in the listing; the cutoff binds the push, not the completion of the check suite, and delay caused by neither party does not defeat payment. (5) Where the reported defect is that an operation is too slow, the listing's stated numeric threshold governs; if the listing states no threshold, this rule does not determine an outcome. If the designated check suite has not reported within fourteen days of the push, and no maintainer has stated a position, pay the full bounty.
rule.notes:
Written against the eight counterexamples that ps_6ce467da9d20c1f2 found in v1.
Each clause exists because a specific probe split the panel: (1) and the override
language answer conflicting_evidence; (2) answers regression_after_fix; (3)
answers partial_completion; (4) answers late_evidence; (5) answers criteria_gap;
the fourteen-day fallback answers missing_confirmation.
Note what this rule deliberately does NOT do: it does not make the deal fairer.
Clause (2) is harsh, and clause (5) leaves a whole class of bounties
undecidable on purpose rather than inventing a threshold. Brightline measures
decidability, not fairness.

disclaimer: Split Score is an experimental measurement of panel divergence over a fixed probe set. It is not a probability that a dispute will occur, not a prediction of how a human court would rule, and not a judgment about whether the agreement is fair. Decidability is not fairness: a rule can be trivially easy to adjudicate and still be one-sided.
